formative_worksheets.title: The Three Pattern Types Check
formative_worksheets.when_to_use: After Lesson 3, before Lesson 4. Quick mid-unit check (12 minutes) to confirm C1.1 (three pattern types), C1.2 (table of values translation), and rule notation have landed before adding far prediction in Lesson 4.
formative_worksheets.purpose: Standalone formative assessment distinct from lesson worksheets. Lets the teacher quickly see which children can identify all three pattern types AND build a table of values, and which need a bridging conversation before Lesson 4's detective + prediction work.
formative_worksheets.student_learning_goal: I can identify the three pattern types AND build a table of values.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can identify the three pattern types AND build a table of values.
header.character_watermark: Coco the Conductor in the top-right corner with a small magnifying glass — the 'check-in' Coco. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

prompts.prompt: Look at each parade. Write the type and the rule on the lines.
prompts.visual_layout: Three short parade strips stacked vertically. Strip A: 4-cell repeating Bea-Finn-Bea-Finn (rule AB). Strip B: 4-cell growing 1, 4, 7, 10 stacked Beas (rule +3). Strip C: 4-cell shrinking 12, 9, 6, 3 stacked Beas (rule -3). Beside each strip, two writing lines: 'Type: ___. Rule: ___.'

image_placeholders.description: A 4-cell horizontal parade strip in B&W line-art. Cells filled in order: Bea, Finn, Bea, Finn (animal AB repeating). Footprints beneath. Labelled 'A' to the left.
A 4-cell horizontal parade strip in matching style with stacked Beas: 1, 4, 7, 10 — visibly growing by 3 per cell. Footprints beneath. Labelled 'B' to the left.
A 4-cell horizontal parade strip in matching style with stacked Beas: 12, 9, 6, 3 — visibly shrinking by 3 per cell. Footprints beneath. Labelled 'C' to the left.

prompts.answer_key: A: Type = REPEATING. Rule = AB. B: Type = GROWING. Rule = +3. C: Type = SHRINKING. Rule = -3. A child who gets all 6 lines correct has Level 3 evidence on C1.1 + C1.3.

prompts.prompt: Build a table of values for this growing pattern. Then write the rule.
prompts.visual_layout: Top: a pre-built 4-cell growing parade (3, 6, 9, 12 stacked Beas — rule +3). Below: an empty 2-column table with TERM and VALUE headers, 4 data rows. Term column pre-filled 1-4. Value column blank. Below the table: 'Rule: +____'.

image_placeholders.description: A 4-cell horizontal parade strip pre-filled with stacked Beas: 3, 6, 9, 12 — a +3 growing pattern. Footprints beneath. Full width.
A 2-column table of values, ~3in wide × 2.5in tall. 5 rows (1 header + 4 data). Headers TERM and VALUE in bold uppercase. Term column pre-filled 1, 2, 3, 4. Value column empty. Thin black borders.

prompts.answer_key: Value column: 3, 6, 9, 12. Rule = +3. Correct if both the table is filled accurately AND the rule label is +3 (or 'three' or 'add 3').

prompts.prompt: How are you feeling about pattern types and tables of values? Circle the face that fits.
prompts.visual_layout: Three faces in a horizontal row: a big smile, a neutral mouth, and a worried frown. Below each face, a label: 'I got it!', 'Almost!', 'Need help!'.

image_placeholders.description: Three round face icons in a horizontal row, each ~1.5in across. Left face: smiling. Middle: neutral. Right: downturned. Labels beneath: 'I got it!', 'Almost!', 'Need help!'. Total row width ~6in. B&W line art.

prompts.answer_key: Open. Use alongside Prompts 1 and 2 to identify mismatches: a child who got Prompt 1 wrong but circled 'I got it!' may need more discussion; a child who got Prompts 1 and 2 right but circled 'Need help!' may just need confidence-building.

formative_worksheets.teacher_notes: Administer this between Lesson 3 and Lesson 4 — it is the 12-minute mid-unit gate. Score guide: 2/2 + correct rule labels + table headers + confident self-rating = ready for Lesson 4. 1/2 + correct table = brief 1:1 conference reviewing the type/rule distinction. Children who left the table value column blank or wrote the term number in the value column need a re-loop on the table-of-values structure before continuing.

reflection_sheet.title: My Pattern Parade Reflection
reflection_sheet.purpose: End-of-unit metacognition. Children look back at their week of pattern work — including the new Grade 2 expectations of growing/shrinking patterns, tables of values, and number patterns to 100 — and rate themselves, name a favourite, name a struggle, and set a forward goal. Companion to the Lesson 5 summative.
reflection_sheet.student_learning_goal: I can think about what I learned this week.

header.student_learning_goal_banner: I can think about what I learned this week.
header.character_watermark: Coco the Conductor in the top-right corner, holding a Junior Pattern Conductor certificate. Small (~1.5in tall). References blueprint.recurring_characters.

prompts.prompt: How do you feel about being a Pattern Conductor? Circle one.
prompts.visual_layout: Three star-rating options shown horizontally, each in its own oval: 1 star, 2 stars, 3 stars. Beneath each oval, a label: 'Just starting', 'Mostly got it', 'I am a Conductor!'.

Each option enclosed in a thin oval ~2in wide × 1.5in tall. Beneath each oval, printed label: 'Just starting', 'Mostly got it', 'I am a Conductor!'. Total row ~6.5in wide. B&W line art only.

prompts.prompt: Did you do these things this week? Circle YES or NO.
prompts.visual_layout: A five-row table. Each row contains a question label on the left and YES / NO bubbles on the right. Questions: 'I identified a repeating, growing, and shrinking pattern.', 'I named a rule using +N or -N notation.', 'I built a table of values with TERM and VALUE columns.', 'I predicted term 10 without drawing it.', 'I built a number parade up to 100.'.

options: I identified a repeating, growing, and shrinking pattern.
I named a rule using +N or -N notation.
I built a table of values with TERM and VALUE columns.
I predicted term 10 without drawing it.
I built a number parade up to 100.

reflection_sheet.teacher_notes: Hand out at the very end of Lesson 5, alongside the Junior Pattern Conductor certificate ceremony. Grade 2 children can write short responses to prompts 3-5 — accept invented spelling. A child who writes only a drawing has a complete answer. Prompt 2 explicitly maps to the new Grade 2 expectations (table of values, far prediction, numbers to 100) so a NO on any of those lines tells you what to revisit before the next pattern unit. The yes/no audit on Prompt 2 is also a quick teacher check: a 'NO' on any item signals the child either missed a key activity or doesn't recognize that they did it.
